subject_recognition.observed: At 270 px each principal object can be named: typing forearms, a clipboard chart with teal tabs, a labelled teal OpenEvidence box, an Answer card with a Sources slot of three chips and a dashed Accuracy box with an empty ring. Also legible: citation cards titled 'Medical literature', 'Clinical guidelines' and 'Other sources' (18-21 s), a board of 12 faceless clinician silhouettes over a 'Half / More than half' bar (22-28 s), and large 'Accuracy / Not in release' and 'Patient care / Not in release' tags (31-32 s). No face or identifiable clinician appears anywhere. The weak spot is 16-17 s: almost all empty floor around an Answer card about 75 px wide, with citation cards that are too small to read until 18 s.

contact_and_consequence.observed: The before and after states are readable. At 0 s fingertips are on the keys with the Question card on the chart. At 1 s the card is off the chart. At 3-4 s the Answer card rests under the tool and gains three source chips. At 11-13 s the masked 'Usual credentials' field fills from 5 to 8 dots under the fingers. At 14-15 s the Question card fills with word bars and a 'Plain language' pill. At 7 and 9 s the date tags hang from pins on the teal 'Health record' boundary. Cards and tags cast soft shadows. The stills show neither the card's flight, the lock opening nor the slide to the chart edge, and no hand touches a card: the send reads as a diagram transfer.

dominant_action.observed: Each change happens on the focal object. At 22-23 s the clinician tiles light from 2 to about 7 of 12 and the bar fills past Half to 'More than half'. A 'Clinical decision support' tag appears at 25 s and a 'UTMB's own report' tag at 28 s. Two limit tags are clipped to the answer at 30 s and fill the frame reading 'Not in release' at 31-32 s. At 34-35 s the Medical literature card is threaded to the Sources slot. At 36-38 s the empty dashed Accuracy ring stays empty and is brighter at 37 s. Frames 19-21 are nearly identical, so the two 'lift' events read as a hold on readable evidence.

surface_finish.observed: The film is a consistent flat editorial illustration: soft card shadows, ruled chart paper, a steel clip and lopsided teal tabs, pinned tags with strings, a plank-lined floor and a window onto a grassy plain with a flat-topped tree. The weakest surfaces are the hands (flat brown fill, tube-like fingers, long forearms leaving the frame at 0-1 and 11-15 s) and the plain bevelled teal tool box. These are flaws in polish, not placeholders. A tag string crosses the Accuracy tag's lettering at 31-32 s and in the close, and a thread crosses 'Answer' at 36-38 s. The 'native' stills are 270x480, so no native-crop finish was inspectable.

continuity.observed: The same chart, tool, answer, citation set and clinician board carry through every cut, and the disclosure pill stays on screen throughout. Two continuity cheats: at 39-41 s the decision and report tags are gone from the bar without being moved on screen, and the 'Evaluating use and experience' tag hangs from the end pin where 'UTMB's own report' hung at 28 s, so the attribution may read as replaced. At the 41.75 s cut the figures drop out and only the bar strip remains at the top edge.

closing_payoff.observed: At 41 s the 'Evaluating use and experience' tag hangs from the More-than-half bar, and below it the OpenEvidence box is cropped to 'penEvidence / tool' under the caption plate. At 42-43 s the frames are identical: the bar and evaluating tag at top, the clipboard chart at left (about 30 percent cropped), and the Answer card with filled Sources chips, an empty dashed Accuracy ring and both Not in release tags. It answers what comes back and shows the published limit without inventing an outcome. It recaps the 31-38 s imagery at a smaller scale, and the 'Not in release' lettering is about 9 px tall.

limits: This review used only the r9 stills: four contact sheets per film at one frame per second (270x480) and the 41 s and 42.9 s stills, which are also 270x480. At this sampling and size I could see no visible difference between these A frames and the earlier r5 A frames, consistent with a punctuation-only repair, and B is unchanged. Motion between frames can't be seen: card and hand paths, the lock opening, glow and pulse timing, velocity or stutter faults. The send (about 0.6-1.5 s), the slide to the chart edge (about 15 s), the citation lifts (18-21 s) and the evaluating-tag settle (39.9-41 s) are judged only from their before and after states. Native-crop finish wasn't inspectable. Sound and sync weren't reviewed. Caption timings are authored estimates. SHA256 values are echoed from the contract, not recomputed. This verdict is a muted phone preflight on these bytes only. It approves no score, take or shipment, and the measured timed phone, native hero, audiovisual and panel reviews still apply.
